title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Determination of the Nature of Illegal Fund-Raising Criminal Cases
keywords_en: Court regarding illegal fundraising criminal cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issues Concerning the Determination of the Nature of Illegal Fundraising Criminal Cases

Fa [2011] No. 262

The High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

For the purpose of lawfully, accurately, and timely adjudicating illegal fundraising criminal cases, notice is hereby given on the relevant issues concerning the determination of the nature of illegal fundraising as follows:

1. The determination of the nature of illegal fundraising by administrative departments is not a necessary procedure for an illegal fundraising case to enter criminal proceedings. The failure of an administrative department to make a determination of the nature of illegal fundraising shall not affect the trial of an illegal fundraising criminal case.

2. A people's court shall, in accordance with the Criminal Law and the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Illegal Fundraising Criminal Cases and other relevant provisions, determine the nature of the facts of the case and determine whether the relevant conduct constitutes a crime.

3. For cases where the facts are complex and the determination of the nature is difficult, a people's court may, on the basis of the administrative determination opinions of the relevant departments on whether the industry technical standards are met, make a determination of the nature in accordance with the facts of the case and the provisions of the law.

4. The trial of illegal fundraising criminal cases involves a wide range of fields and is highly specialized. People's courts, in adjudicating such cases, shall pay attention to strengthening coordination with the relevant competent (supervisory) administrative departments, public security organs, and people's procuratorates. If major issues are encountered in the trial work that are difficult to resolve, please promptly report to the Supreme People's Court.

August 18, 2011
